name: The Content Engine: 12 Solo Founder Prompts
tagline: Turn a single idea into a full week of high-converting social media posts in minutes.
metaDescription: Stop staring at a blank screen. Use these 12 plug-and-play AI prompts to transform one core idea into a full week of engaging content for solo founders.
description:
If you are a solo founder wearing every hat, content creation often feels like a full-time distraction rather than a growth lever. You have the product insights and the vision, but translating that into a consistent daily posting schedule is exhausting. This digital toolkit solves the blank-page syndrome by giving you a reliable system to multiply your output. Instead of starting from scratch every morning, you feed an AI one core insight, opinion, or product update, and run it through this curated sequence of 12 modular prompts. 

These prompts work because they are engineered specifically for the constraints and goals of bootstrapped founders. They avoid generic marketing fluff, focusing instead on narrative hooks, customer pain points, behind-the-scenes building, and direct calls to action. Each prompt is designed with strict structural constraints to ensure the AI output sounds human, authoritative, and tailored to platforms like LinkedIn and X. Whether you are launching a new feature, sharing a revenue milestone, or breaking down an industry myth, this system keeps your brand top-of-mind without demanding hours of your day.
includes: 1 PDF guide with implementation instructions and usage tips
1 Notion workspace containing all 12 ready-to-use prompts
Categorized into Launch, Thought Leadership, and Build in Public
sampleItems: Write a contrarian industry take based on this core belief: [Insert Core Belief]. Structure the post with a sharp one-sentence hook, three bullet points explaining why the conventional wisdom is broken, and a concluding question to drive comments from target users.

Draft a 'Build in Public' update focusing on this recent challenge: [Insert Challenge]. Share the raw problem, the immediate mistake made, the lesson learned, and the exact metric or outcome. Tone should be transparent, humble, and analytical.

items.title: The Contrarian Take
items.body: Write a contrarian industry take based on this core belief: [Insert Core Belief]. Structure the post with a sharp one-sentence hook, three bullet points explaining why the conventional wisdom is broken, and a concluding question to drive comments from target users. Keep the tone pragmatic, confident, and direct, avoiding buzzwords or corporate jargon entirely.

items.title: The Build in Public Mistake
items.body: Draft a behind-the-scenes update focusing on this recent challenge or failure: [Insert Challenge]. Share the raw problem, the immediate mistake made, the lesson learned, and the exact metric or outcome. Tone should be transparent, humble, and analytical. End with a takeaway for other bootstrap founders facing similar hurdles.

items.title: The Customer Pain Point Story
items.body: Transform this customer frustration: [Insert Frustration] into a mini case study or narrative post. Start with the exhausting manual process your target audience deals with daily. Introduce your product not as a hero, but as the practical key that unlocked efficiency. Include a clear before-and-after contrast without sounding overly salesy.

items.title: The Feature Breakdown
items.body: Take this specific product feature or update: [Insert Feature] and explain it through the lens of 'What it lets you do that you couldn't do yesterday.' Write a short, punchy post featuring a step-by-step implementation guide in three easy bullet points. Focus purely on utility and time-saved for busy solo operators.

items.title: The Framework Share
items.body: Convert this mental model or workflow I use in my business: [Insert Workflow] into an actionable framework post. Break it down into named sequential steps. Explain the 'why' behind each step briefly so readers can immediately apply the exact same process to their own solo operations today.

items.title: The Metric Milestone
items.body: Write a reflective milestone post about reaching this target: [Insert Metric]. Avoid pure vanity flexing by breaking down the two specific, unglamorous actions that actually drove the result. Share one thing that failed along the way so other founders get practical value from your win.

items.title: The FAQ Authority Post
items.body: Take the most common question prospects ask before buying: [Insert Question] and write a definitive, no-nonsense answer. Address the hidden skepticism behind the question, explain your philosophy clearly, and position your product as a logical extension of that worldview.

items.title: The Micro-Case Study
items.body: Write a short social post highlighting how a specific type of user achieved a specific result using [Insert Product]. Structure it as: The Situation, The Action, The Result. Keep it under 150 words to maximize readability and impact on mobile feeds.

items.title: The Industry Prediction
items.body: Analyze this emerging trend or shift in our market: [Insert Trend]. State clearly what will happen over the next 12 months, why most incumbents will miss it, and how solo founders can position themselves to capitalize on the shift right now. Keep the prose sharp and authoritative.

items.title: The Founder Routine
items.body: Detail a specific productivity hack, automation, or time-management routine you use to keep your solo business running while protecting your sanity: [Insert Routine]. Explain the setup, the tools involved, and the exact time savings it provides every single week.

items.title: The Direct Pitch
items.body: Write a high-converting, direct promotional post for [Insert Product]. Focus on the primary pain point, introduce the solution, list three concrete benefits with checkmarks, and end with a clear, low-friction call to action directing readers to the link in the comments.

items.title: The Lesson Learned
items.body: Reflect on a hard lesson learned over the past month of running your solo business: [Insert Lesson]. Frame the narrative around 'What I wish I knew six months ago.' Keep the tone reflective, encouraging, and focused on helping early-stage founders avoid the same trap.
